# A note from Linden & Rye about our prices

*Posted on the window and on the Instagram account of Linden & Rye, a neighbourhood café and bakery. Fictional document written as an example seed for Tellfold.*

Dear neighbours,

We opened Linden & Rye on Alder Street nine years ago with one oven, four tables and a sourdough starter called Gus. Many of you have been coming since the first week. Some of you met your partners here. Some of you have written whole theses at the corner table. Thank you.

We have kept our prices the same for three years. In that time, butter has gone up 61%, flour 38%, coffee beans 45% and our rent 22%. We also raised every team member's pay to at least €15 an hour last spring, which we are proud of and will not undo.

So, starting **Monday 2 March**, some prices will change:

- Filter coffee: €2.40 to €2.90
- Flat white: €3.60 to €4.20
- Sourdough loaf: €5.50 to €6.80
- Cinnamon bun: €3.20 to €3.90
- Lunch soup with bread: €7.50 to €8.90

Some things are **not** changing:

- Day-old bread stays at half price after 4 pm.
- The pay-it-forward board stays. You can still buy a coffee for someone who needs one.
- Refills of filter coffee stay free.

Some things are new:

- A **neighbour card** for €12 a month: one filter coffee every day. If you come in most mornings, it will cost you less than before.
- From April we will close on **Tuesdays** as well as Mondays, so our small team gets two days off together.

We know nobody likes paying more, especially now. We thought about using cheaper butter and smaller buns instead, and decided we would rather be honest with you about the price than quietly make things worse.

# Mossbook is changing how it's priced. Here's what that means for you.

*Posted by Ines Okafor-Brandt, co-founder of Mossbook Labs, on the Mossbook blog. Fictional document written as an example seed for Tellfold.*

Six years ago, two of us built Mossbook in a rented garage because our own houseplants kept dying. The idea was simple: take a photo of a plant, get a care plan, get reminded when it needs water, light or a new pot. We sold it for a one-time price of $24.99, and about 410,000 of you bought it. Thank you. That one purchase has paid for six years of updates, a plant-identification model that now knows more than 9,000 species, and a team that grew from two people to nineteen.

Today we're announcing the biggest change we have ever made to Mossbook, and we want to explain it plainly.

## What is changing

Starting **March 3**, new users will download Mossbook for free and can track up to five plants without paying. To go beyond five plants, or to use the features listed below, they'll need **Mossbook Plus**, which costs **$3.99 a month or $29.99 a year**.

Mossbook Plus includes:

- Unlimited plants and rooms
- Photo diagnosis ("why are the leaves on my fiddle-leaf fig turning brown?"), which runs on our servers
- Weather-aware watering for balcony and garden plants
- Household sharing for up to six people
- The new Grow Journal with time-lapse photos

## What happens to people who already paid

This is the part we argued about the most, so here it is in detail.

If you bought Mossbook at any point before March 3, you keep everything you have today, forever. Unlimited plants, reminders, the species library, offline mode. None of it will move behind the subscription.

Last year these two features cost more than the app earned from new sales.

## Why we're doing this

The honest answer is that one-time pricing worked when Mossbook was an app that lived entirely on your phone. It no longer is. The features people tell us they love most are the ones that run on servers, and servers bill us every month whether or not anyone buys the app that month.

We looked at alternatives. We could have added ads, but nobody wants a banner for fertilizer spikes between them and their monstera. We could have sold your plant data to garden retailers, and we will never do that. We could have kept prices as they are and slowly stopped improving the app, which is what happens to a lot of one-time-purchase apps. We think a small subscription is the most honest of those options.

# Letter to parents: phones at Westbrook Secondary from September

*Sent by email and printed in the school newsletter of Westbrook Secondary School. Fictional document written as an example seed for Tellfold.*

Dear parents and carers,

After a year of discussion with staff, students and the parents' council, Westbrook will become a **phone-free school day** from the start of the autumn term on 3 September.

## What will happen

- Students may still bring a phone to school.
- On arrival, phones are switched off and locked in a personal pouch. The pouch stays with the student, but it can only be opened at the unlocking stations by the main gate at the end of the day.
- This applies during lessons, breaks and lunch, for all year groups (ages 11 to 18).
- Sixth-form students (ages 16 to 18) may unlock their phones in the sixth-form common room during free periods.
- Pouches cost the school €18 each. We will not ask families to pay for them.

## Why we are doing this

In a survey last spring, 64% of our students said they feel pressure to reply to messages during the school day, and 41% said they had seen something upsetting on a phone at school in the last month. Teachers report that lessons regularly stop because of phones. Three schools nearby made the same change last year and report calmer breaks and fewer incidents of online bullying during school hours.

## Contacting your child

If you need to reach your child during the day, call the school office on 01 555 0192 and we will pass on the message straight away. Students with medical needs that rely on a phone (for example glucose monitoring) will be exempt; please contact Ms Duarte, our pastoral lead, before 1 August.

## What happens if a student breaks the rule

# Coming back together: our new working week from 1 June

*Sent by email to all staff of Halden Freight Software, a 140-person logistics software company, by its chief executive. Fictional document written as an example seed for Tellfold.*

Hi everyone,

Since 2021 most of us have worked from home most of the time, and the work has been good. We shipped the new route planner, we kept every big customer and we hired 50 people, half of whom have never met the other half.

That last part is the problem. Onboarding now takes our new engineers about five months, against two and a half before 2020. Support and engineering mostly talk through tickets. In the staff survey in March, 41% said they did not feel part of a team, and only 23% had met their manager's manager in person.

So, from **Monday 1 June**, our working week changes:

- **Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday are office days** for everyone who lives within 90 minutes of the Ostbrück office.
- Monday and Friday stay home days. No meetings before 10 am on any day.
- The **12 people hired as fully remote** stay fully remote. Their teams will meet in person one week each quarter, and we pay for the travel.
- Product, engineering and support **move into mixed teams** of 8 to 10, each owning one part of the product, with one shared desk area per team.
- Two managers' roles change: support and engineering now report to the same head of product, Mareike Lindqvist.

What we are adding:

- A €90 monthly travel allowance for office days, paid with salary.
- Lunch in the office on all three days.
- The second floor becomes quiet space: no calls, no meetings.

What we are not doing:

- A €90 monthly travel allowance for office days, paid with salary.
- Lunch in the office on all three days.
- The second floor becomes quiet space: no calls, no meetings.

What we are not doing:

- Nobody will be tracked by badge swipes or laptop activity.
- Nobody's pay or job depends on the office move.
- If the office days make your caring duties or health harder, talk to People Team before 15 May. We will agree an exception, in writing, with no questions about the details.

I know some of you moved further away during the last five years because you could. If that is you, please talk to us before you decide anything. We would rather find a way than lose you.

We will look at the survey numbers again in December and change this if it is not working. There is an open Q&A on Thursday 7 May at 4 pm, in the office and on video.

Jonas Reuter
Chief executive, Halden Freight Software

# Mossbook is changing how it's priced. Here's what that means for you.

Six years ago, two of us built Mossbook in a rented garage because our own houseplants kept dying. The idea was simple: take a photo of a plant, get a care plan, get reminded when it needs water, light or a new pot.

We sold it for a one-time price of $24.99, and about 410,000 of you bought it. Thank you.

That one purchase has paid for six years of updates, a plant-identification model that now knows more than 9,000 species, and a team that grew from two people to nineteen.

Today we're announcing the biggest change we have ever made to Mossbook, and we want to explain it plainly.

## What is changing

## What is changing

Starting **March 3**, new users will download Mossbook for free and can track up to five plants without paying. To go beyond five plants, or to use the features listed below, they'll need **Mossbook Plus**, which costs **$3.99 a month or $29.99 a year**.

Mossbook Plus includes:

Mossbook Plus includes:

- Unlimited plants and rooms
- Photo diagnosis ("why are the leaves on my fiddle-leaf fig turning brown?"), which runs on our servers
- Weather-aware watering for balcony and garden plants
- Household sharing for up to six people
- The new Grow Journal with

- The new Grow Journal with

time-lapse photos

## What happens to people who already paid

This is the part we argued about the most, so here it is in detail.

the most, so here it is in detail.

If you bought Mossbook at any point before March 3, you keep everything you have today, forever. Unlimited plants, reminders, the species library, offline mode. None of it will move behind the subscription.

it will move behind the subscription.

On top of that, every existing buyer gets **one full year of Mossbook Plus for free**, starting March 3. After that year you can subscribe at a lifetime discount of $17.99 a year, or simply keep using the version you paid for.

Two features will be Plus-only for everyone after the free year ends: photo diagnosis and weather-aware watering. Both of these cost us real money every time you use them.

Photo diagnosis alone runs about 2.1 million image checks a month on rented GPUs, and the weather data comes from a commercial provider that bills us per request. Last year these two features cost more than the app earned from new sales.

## Why we're doing this

The honest answer is that one-time pricing worked when Mossbook was an app that lived entirely on your phone. It no longer is.

The features people tell us they love most are the ones that run on servers, and servers bill us every month whether or not anyone buys the app that month.

on any plan, including the free one. 2.

and without a subscription. 3.

**We'll publish our numbers.** Once a quarter we will post how many people pay for Plus and what we spent on servers, so you can see where the money goes.

The update with the new plans goes out on March 3 for iOS and Android. The free year for existing buyers will be applied automatically; you don't need to do anything. If it doesn't show up, write to support and a human will fix it within a day.

We've changed our plans because of your feedback before, and we'll do it again.

Thank you for six years of dead-plant rescues, very blurry leaf photos, and kind emails.

Ines and the Mossbook team

*Posted on the window and on the Instagram account of Linden & Rye, a neighbourhood café and bakery.

Fictional document written as an example seed for Tellfold.*

Dear neighbours,
We opened Linden & Rye on Alder Street nine years ago with one oven, four tables and a sourdough starter called Gus.
Many of you have been coming since the first week. Some of you met your partners here.

Some of you have written whole theses at the corner table. Thank you.

We have kept our prices the same for three years.
In that time, butter has gone up 61%, flour 38%, coffee beans 45% and our rent 22%.
We also raised every team member's pay to at least €15 an hour last spring, which we are proud of and will not undo.
So, starting **Monday 2 March**, some prices will change:

- Filter coffee: €2.40 to €2.90
- Flat white: €3.60 to €4.20
- Sourdough loaf: €5.50 to €6.80
- Cinnamon bun: €3.20 to

€3.90
- Lunch soup with bread: €7.50 to €8.90

Some things are **not** changing:
- Day-old bread stays at half price after 4 pm. - The pay-it-forward board stays.

You can still buy a coffee for someone who needs one. - Refills of filter coffee stay free.

Some things are new:
- A **neighbour card** for €12 a month: one filter coffee every day.
If you come in most mornings, it will cost you less than before.
- From April we will close on **Tuesdays** as well as Mondays, so our small team gets two days off together.
We know nobody likes paying more, especially now.
We thought about using cheaper butter and smaller buns instead, and decided we would rather be honest with you about
the price than quietly make things worse.
If you have questions, ask any of us at the counter, or come to the open evening on Thursday 26 February at 7 pm.

There will be free buns, and we will listen.

With flour on our hands,
Tomás and Hanna, Linden & Rye
# Consultation: making Market Street car-free
*Published by Fenwick Town Council's transport committee for public consultation.

Fictional document written as an example seed for Tellfold.*

## The proposal
From **1 May next year**, the 400-metre stretch of Market Street between the Clock Tower and Bridge Road would close
to private cars between 10 am and 7 pm, every day of the week. The council would:

- widen the pavements and add 60 trees, benches and space for café seating;
- keep access for buses, taxis, bicycles,
the 48 on-street parking spaces, and reduce the price of the Riverside car park (5 minutes' walk away, 320 spaces)

from €2.50 to €1.50 an hour for the first two hours;
- run a free electric shuttle every 12 minutes between the train
station, the Riverside car park and the Clock Tower.
The scheme would cost €3.1 million, of which €2.4 million comes from a national active-travel grant that must be spent

by the end of next year.

## Why
Market Street carries about 9,000 cars a day, but traffic counts show that around 60% are driving through, not
stopping. Air quality on the street broke the legal limit for nitrogen dioxide on 31 days last year.
Footfall in the town centre has fallen 18% in five years.
Towns of a similar size that pedestrianised their main street report footfall rising 10% to 30% within two years,

although some shops in those towns closed during the building works.

## What we have heard so far
In early conversations, some shop owners told us they worry that customers who drive will go to the out-of-town retail
park instead. Disability groups asked about drop-off points.
Residents of the side streets asked whether traffic will move onto their roads.

The council has commissioned a traffic study and will publish it before a final vote.

## Timeline
- Consultation open now, closes 30 November. - Final council vote: 14 January.
- Works, if approved: February to April, carried out at night where possible.
You can respond online, at the library, or at the drop-in sessions at the town hall on 12 and 19 November.
# Mossbook is changing how it's priced. Here's what that means for you.
*Posted by Ines Okafor-Brandt, co-founder of Mossbook Labs, on the Mossbook blog.
Fictional document written as an example seed for Tellfold.*
Six years ago, two of us built Mossbook in a rented garage because our own houseplants kept dying.
The idea was simple: take a photo of a plant, get a care plan, get reminded when it needs water, light or a new pot.
We sold it for a one-time price of $24.99, and about 410,000 of you bought it. Thank you.
That one purchase has paid for six years of updates, a plant-identification model that now knows more than 9,000
species, and a team that grew from two people to nineteen.
Today we're announcing the biggest change we have ever made to Mossbook, and we want to explain it plainly.
## What is changing
Starting **March 3**, new users will download Mossbook for free and can track up to five plants without paying.
To go beyond five plants, or to use the features listed below, they'll need **Mossbook Plus**, which costs **$3.99 a

month or $29.99 a year**.

Mossbook Plus includes:

- Unlimited plants and rooms
- Photo diagnosis ("why are the leaves on my fiddle-leaf fig turning brown?"), which runs

on our servers
- Weather-aware watering for balcony and garden plants
- Household sharing for up to six people
- The

new Grow Journal with time-lapse photos

## What happens to people who already paid
This is the part we argued about the most, so here it is in detail.
If you bought Mossbook at any point before March 3, you keep everything you have today, forever.
Unlimited plants, reminders, the species library, offline mode. None of it will move behind the subscription.
On top of that, every existing buyer gets **one full year of Mossbook Plus for free**, starting March 3.
After that year you can subscribe at a lifetime discount of $17.99 a year, or simply keep using the version you paid

for.

Two features will be Plus-only for everyone after the free year ends: photo diagnosis and weather-aware watering.
Both of these cost us real money every time you use them.
Photo diagnosis alone runs about 2.1 million image checks a month on rented GPUs, and the weather data comes from a
commercial provider that bills us per request.

Last year these two features cost more than the app earned from new sales.

## Why we're doing this
The honest answer is that one-time pricing worked when Mossbook was an app that lived entirely on your phone.
It no longer is.
The features people tell us they love most are the ones that run on servers, and servers bill us every month whether

or not anyone buys the app that month.

We looked at alternatives.
We could have added ads, but nobody wants a banner for fertilizer spikes between them and their monstera.
We could have sold your plant data to garden retailers, and we will never do that.
We could have kept prices as they are and slowly stopped improving the app, which is what happens to a lot of

one-time-purchase apps. We think a small subscription is the most honest of those options.

## What we're committing to

We know a pricing change asks you to trust us, so here are commitments you can hold us to:

1.
**Your data stays yours.** You can export all of your plants, photos and journal entries as a ZIP file at any time, on
any plan, including the free one. 2.
**Offline mode stays free.** Reminders and care plans will always work without an internet connection and without a
subscription. 3.
**No price increase for current subscribers before 2028.** If we ever raise prices, anyone already subscribed keeps
their price. 4.
**Student and community-garden discount.** Verified students and registered community gardens get Plus for $9.99 a
year. 5.
**We'll publish our numbers.** Once a quarter we will post how many people pay for Plus and what we spent on servers,

so you can see where the money goes.

## What's next
The update with the new plans goes out on March 3 for iOS and Android.
The free year for existing buyers will be applied automatically; you don't need to do anything.
If it doesn't show up, write to support and a human will fix it within a day.
We're also hosting an open Q&A on our community forum on February 24, where the whole team will answer questions for

as long as people have them. Bring the hard ones.

We know some of you will be disappointed.
Some of you bought Mossbook precisely because it wasn't a subscription, and we respect that.
We've tried to make sure that nobody who already paid loses anything they paid for.
If we got something wrong, tell us. We've changed our plans because of your feedback before, and we'll do it again.

Thank you for six years of dead-plant rescues, very blurry leaf photos, and kind emails.

Ines and the Mossbook team
# Letter to parents: phones at Westbrook Secondary from September
*Sent by email and printed in the school newsletter of Westbrook Secondary School.

Fictional document written as an example seed for Tellfold.*

Dear parents and carers,
After a year of discussion with staff, students and the parents' council, Westbrook will become a **phone-free school

day** from the start of the autumn term on 3 September.

## What will happen
- Students may still bring a phone to school. - On arrival, phones are switched off and locked in a personal pouch.
The pouch stays with the student, but it can only be opened at the unlocking stations by the main gate at the end of
the day. - This applies during lessons, breaks and lunch, for all year groups (ages 11 to 18).
- Sixth-form students (ages 16 to 18) may unlock their phones in the sixth-form common room during free periods.

- Pouches cost the school €18 each. We will not ask families to pay for them.

## Why we are doing this
In a survey last spring, 64% of our students said they feel pressure to reply to messages during the school day, and
41% said they had seen something upsetting on a phone at school in the last month.
Teachers report that lessons regularly stop because of phones.
Three schools nearby made the same change last year and report calmer breaks and fewer incidents of online bullying

during school hours.

## Contacting your child
If you need to reach your child during the day, call the school office on 01 555 0192 and we will pass on the message
straight away.
Students with medical needs that rely on a phone (for example glucose monitoring) will be exempt; please contact Ms

Duarte, our pastoral lead, before 1 August.

## What happens if a student breaks the rule
The first time, the phone is kept at the office until the end of the day.

After the third time in a term, a parent or carer must collect it in person.

## Have your say
We know some of you have concerns, especially about travel to and from school, and about emergencies.
Please join us at the information evening on **Tuesday 17 June at 6:30 pm** in the main hall, or reply to this email.

Yours sincerely,
Dr Amara Lewis, Headteacher
# Coming back together: our new working week from 1 June
*Sent by email to all staff of Halden Freight Software, a 140-person logistics software company, by its chief

executive. Fictional document written as an example seed for Tellfold.*

Hi everyone,
Since 2021 most of us have worked from home most of the time, and the work has been good.
We shipped the new route planner, we kept every big customer and we hired 50 people, half of whom have never met the

other half.

That last part is the problem.
Onboarding now takes our new engineers about five months, against two and a half before 2020.
Support and engineering mostly talk through tickets.
In the staff survey in March, 41% said they did not feel part of a team, and only 23% had met their manager's manager

in person.

So, from **Monday 1 June**, our working week changes:
- **Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday are office days** for everyone who lives within 90 minutes of the Ostbrück office.
- Monday and Friday stay home days. No meetings before 10 am on any day.
- The **12 people hired as fully remote** stay fully remote.
Their teams will meet in person one week each quarter, and we pay for the travel.
- Product, engineering and support **move into mixed teams** of 8 to 10, each owning one part of the product, with one
shared desk area per team.
- Two managers' roles change: support and engineering now report to the same head of product, Mareike Lindqvist.
What we are adding:
- A €90 monthly travel allowance for office days, paid with salary. - Lunch in the office on all three days.

- The second floor becomes quiet space: no calls, no meetings.

What we are not doing:
- Nobody will be tracked by badge swipes or laptop activity. - Nobody's pay or job depends on the office move.
- If the office days make your caring duties or health harder, talk to People Team before 15 May.
We will agree an exception, in writing, with no questions about the details.
I know some of you moved further away during the last five years because you could.
If that is you, please talk to us before you decide anything. We would rather find a way than lose you.
We will look at the survey numbers again in December and change this if it is not working.
There is an open Q&A on Thursday 7 May at 4 pm, in the office and on video.

Jonas Reuter
Chief executive, Halden Freight Software
